title: Discovery and structure-activity relationship of cannabidiol aminoquinones as anti-Alzheimer's agents via dual modulation of Nrf2/HO-1 and TLR4/NF-kappaB pathways.
authors: Zhang, Ziwen; Gao, Shan; Zhao, Jie; Liu, Xiaodan; Zuo, Fangfang; Wu, Yinxin; Ai, Ling; Tang, Wenjian
one_liner_zh: 该文研究大麻二酚氨基醌类化合物通过Nrf2/HO-1和TLR4/NF-kappaB通路抗阿尔茨海默病，分子对接仅针对小分子-蛋白，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Neuroinflammation and oxidative stress are recognized as key drivers of neuronal death and the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. At the same time, they serve as central hubs linking the major pathological hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease (AD), including Abeta aggregation, tau protein hyperphosphorylation, neurofibrillary tangle formation, and neuronal injury. In this study, we screened natural active molecules of cannabidiol (CBD) and its derivatives, and conducted molecular docking simulations. A class of CBD aminoquinone scaffolds with potential anti-AD activity was identified, and 32 CBD aminoquinone derivatives were synthesized for comprehensive in vitro and in vivo evaluation. Among them, compound G-12 with p-F-aniline moiety exhibited potent anti-inflammatory activity (IC(50) = 1.39 muM), outstanding neuroprotective effects (IC(50) = 1.29 muM), and prominent behavioral manifestations. In addition, G-12 displayed acceptable in vivo pharmacokinetic (PK) properties. The superior performance of G-12 indicated that through the Nrf2/HO-1 oxidative stress pathway, it affected the TLR4/NF-kappaB inflammatory pathway, inhibited neuroinflammation, and thereby influenced Abeta aggregation, protecting neurons. This strategy that links several major pathological features of AD is effective in combating AD. G-12 is also a lead compound with the potential to be developed into a multifunctional drug for AD.
abstract_zh: 神经炎症和氧化应激被认为是神经元死亡及神经退行性疾病进展的关键驱动因素。同时，它们作为连接阿尔茨海默病（AD）主要病理标志的核心枢纽，包括Aβ聚集、tau蛋白过度磷酸化、神经原纤维缠结形成和神经元损伤。在本研究中，我们筛选了大麻二酚（CBD）及其衍生物的天然活性分子，并进行了分子对接模拟。鉴定出一类具有潜在抗AD活性的CBD氨基醌骨架，并合成了32种CBD氨基醌衍生物，用于全面的体外和体内评估。其中，含有对氟苯胺部分的化合物G-12表现出强效的抗炎活性（IC(50) = 1.39 μM）、卓越的神经保护作用（IC(50) = 1.29 μM）以及显著的行为学表现。此外，G-12显示出可接受的体内药代动力学（PK）特性。G-12的优越性能表明，它通过Nrf2/HO-1氧化应激通路影响TLR4/NF-κB炎症通路，抑制神经炎症，从而影响Aβ聚集，保护神经元。这种连接AD多个主要病理特征的策略在对抗AD方面是有效的。G-12也是一种具有开发成多功能AD药物潜力的先导化合物。
